t: Tikal, ancient Mutal, was one of the two great powers of the Classic Maya, a city of tens of thousands in Guatemala's Petén forest.
In 378 a warrior linked with Teotihuacan remade its dynasty, and its long rivalry with the Snake kingdom of Calakmul shaped Maya politics.
Victories in 695 and 743–744 restored its power in an age of giant temples, but its kings vanished in the ninth-century collapse.
dyk: Carved wooden lintels from Tikal's Temple IV, one of them celebrating a victory of 743, were taken to Switzerland in 1877 and are still in a museum in Basel.
ev: Yax Ehb Xook, later honoured as founder of the royal line, rules at Tikal
